items.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV$\cdot$cm, $>$20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show $2.9 \pm 0.2$ dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.

items.zh_full: Penguin Solutions于11月4日宣布，已达成最终协议，将其Cree LED业务出售给私募股权公司Transom Capital Group（Transom）。Cree LED长期以来在行业中扮演重要角色，是将LED技术引入通用照明应用的先驱之一。TrendForce认为，所有权的变更可能使该公司能够更加专注于其核心LED业务，未来的产品策略可能会强调发光效率、成本竞争力以及全面的照明解决方案。此次交易使Cree LED重新受到关注，并引发了对照明LED供应链的讨论。TrendForce指出，这一变动可能对LED供应链的竞争格局产生影响，尤其是在通用照明领域。Cree LED作为行业先驱，其技术积累和市场地位在LED照明发展中具有重要历史意义。此次出售后，新所有者可能调整业务方向，但具体战略细节尚未公布。TrendForce将持续关注该交易对LED产业的影响。

items.title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas. The measured beam steering efficiency of such a volume gas grating exceeds 90% that makes this approach a candidate for producing other large-aperture, high-throughput molecular optics elements, with expected damage thresholds 0.5-1 kJ/cm2, much-needed for future ultrahigh-power lasers.

items.title: Hysteresis and mode switching in FIB engineered random laser diodes
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex dynamical behavior in laser diodes is commonly induced by external perturbations such as optical or optoelectronic feedback and optical injection. The structural transformation of a stable laser diode into a stand-alone nonlinear dynamical system would provide a practical alternative as a single and compact device. Here we demonstrate the fabrication of such a device by milling, via focused ion beam, the output facet of a Fabry-Perot laser diode with a predesigned mask, obtaining a scattering surface which provide feedback for random lasing. The fabricated random laser diode shows multi-mode emission with current dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum and mode switching at constant bias current. We attribute this behavior to the interplay between scattered optical feedback and carrier induced local variations of refractive index and temperature at the output facet surface, where defects are located. The observed phenomena reveal complex nonlinear behavior emerging from a single standalone device, which could be tailored by varying the milling pattern, thereby providing a flexible platform for different applications.

items.title: Universal spectral shapes of nonlinear light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operating within the framework of the collisionless Boltzmann equation, we identify universal spectral profiles inherent in stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings and derive physically intuitive solutions for such spectral shapes, expressing them in a manifestly causal closed form that satisfies the Kramers - Kronig relations and fulfills the fluctuation - dissipation theorem. Benchmarking against gold-standard experiments on dilute-gas stimulated light scattering verifies a high descriptive and explanatory power of these solutions and demonstrates their ability to isolate universality motifs in nonlinear scattering spectra as the key to fully understanding the physics behind dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering. As one of important outcomes, such analysis reveals the physical content of the bandwidth of dilute-gas nonlinear scattering spectra as an expression and a quantifier of the phase-mixing time, i.e., the time required for free-streaming gas particles with a mean thermal velocity to traverse the distance equal to the spacing of the laser-driven density grating.

items.title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moir\'e Light Fields
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moir\'e superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moir\'e spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.

items.title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.

items.title: Revisiting the dispersions and quality factors of nanoshell plasmons
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. We find that prior theoretical works, focused primarily on the thin-nanoshell and retarded regimes, obtained qualitatively incorrect results for both the plasmonic dispersions and the associated plasmonic quality factors. Some of these errors have been pointed out in subsequent works, though the corrected results have not been reported, to our knowledge. Beyond obtaining the correct results (correct dispersions and quality factors as a function of nanoshell thickness), we scrutinize the assumption (used by many prior works) that Matthiessen's rule may be used to combine the effects of bulk and surface-mediated plasmonic scattering processes. To do so, we extend prior work by Dingle to the nanoshell geometry. Although we find qualitative agreement with the Matthiessen's rule approach, we find that Dingle's theory systematically predicts higher quality factors across the range of nanoshell thicknesses we consider.

items.title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.

items.title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.13743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the complex full-vector modal field evolution in tapered spun ring-core fiber amplifiers subject to structural perturbations, utilizing a combined coupled-mode theory and rate-equation model. To provide a comprehensive characterization, we introduce a normalized complex modal-state fidelity factor that simultaneously incorporates intensity, phase and polarization into a single quantitative measure. We demonstrate that the twist pitch of the structure can be purposely tuned to either suppress or leverage the effect of specific geometrical perturbations. These findings provide insight into the physical conditions governing modal stability, establishing a robust mechanism for highly efficient in-fiber OAM mode conversion.

items.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

items.title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.

items.title: An Alignment Microscope for Imaging Rotational Wavepacket Dynamics
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new method for encoding polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals directly into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond laser beam. The approach employs a pump-probe setup in a common-path geometry. A radial-azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to $2\pi$ within a single transverse beam profile. Consequently, the angular dependence of the molecular response can be recorded simultaneously rather than reconstructed through sequential measurements at different polarization angles. By varying only the pump-probe delay, this spatial encoding enables single-shot acquisition of the complete angular response at each delay and real-time visualization of the evolving molecular alignment pattern as the delay stage is scanned. This technique has enabled the experimental realization of an alignment microscope.

items.title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. Multi-field point spread functions (PSFs) from a dedicated test configuration characterize misalignment, while golden-sample reference calibration and unified regression predict adjustments toward a common optical target across toleranced specimens. In simulations with tolerances, one step reduced the mean differential wavefront RMS from $0.0592\lambda$ to $0.0086\lambda$, an 85.4% reduction. In alignment experiments on 100 production subgroups, SGAA increased the mean full-lens weighted modulation transfer function (WMTF) at 30, 50, and 80 lp/mm by 0.073, 0.065, and 0.040, respectively, relative to industrial MTF-based scanning. The 8 MP acceptance yield increased by 29.2 percentage points, and mean alignment time decreased from 43 s to 3.1 s. SGAA thus translates independent subgroup reference-state restoration into gains in full-lens imaging, acceptance yield, and alignment speed.

items.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical. In four dimensions, incorporating the pulse-duration scaling and a square-root transformation of conversion efficiency further improves the accuracy of the reconstructed landscape, as validated against an independent reference dataset. We also employ a threshold-based acquisition strategy to identify extended high-efficiency operating regions rather than isolated optimal points. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating physical knowledge into Bayesian optimization improves the exploration and reconstruction of multidimensional high-order harmonic generation landscapes, extending its capabilities beyond locating individual optima.

items.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to $1/T$ as the switching time $T$ tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.

items.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.

items.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

items.title: Background-free and laser-ionization minimized single-shot fs-EFISH in luminous pulsed plasmas
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work introduces spectrally tuned electric field induced second harmonic (t-EFISH) generation for substantially reducing or eliminating background plasma emission in single-shot, time-resolved, electric field measurements. The technique is demonstrated using a femtosecond 1240 nm pump and 620 nm signal detection to avoid spectral and temporal overlap with the early, intense onset of N2(C-B) emission in nanosecond atmospheric-pressure air spark discharges. This enhances signal-to-emission ratios pre- and post-breakdown, enables lower pump energies, suppresses detector saturation, and reduces the coefficient of variation in the electric field measurements by 8.5x. This strategy also provides a pathway for background-free measurements in other discharge environments with varying spectro-temporal emission characteristics. Moreover, the longer 1240 nm pump wavelength reduces multiphoton intrusiveness, directly improving measurement fidelity.

items.title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.

items.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $\mu$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $\mu$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $\mu$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $\mu$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.

items.title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transferring atomic quantum sensors from laboratory-scale physics packages to compact, alignment-free sensor heads suitable for field and space deployment requires a structural platform that combines mechanical, thermal, and optical functionality within a single, manufacturable component. We present such a platform based on additively manufactured technical ceramics: lithography-based ceramic manufacturing is used to fabricate monolithic micro-optical benches with application-specific mounting geometries, while high-precision active alignment and adhesive bonding realize long-term stable optical assemblies through micro-integration. As a first system-level demonstrator, we present a micro-integrated optical frequency reference based on Doppler-free spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 line, integrated within a 6 mL Al2O3 module. A laser stabilized to the reference reaches a fractional frequency instability of $3\times10^{-12}$ at 1 s. We extend the platform to a compact optically pumped magnetometer, exploiting the magnetic cleanliness and tailored thermal properties of high-purity ceramics for a 7 mL sensor head with picotesla sensitivity aimed at space-borne biomagnetometry, and to a micro-integrated optical dipole trap with active MEMS-mirror beam steering for cold-atom manipulation. Together, these demonstrators show that ceramic additive manufacturing and optical micro-integration form a versatile, robust platform for compact atomic sensor systems in field and space applications.

items.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.

items.title: CV-TF-QKD
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrt{\eta}$, where $\eta$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.

items.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.

items.zh_full: 《自然·光子学》于2026年10月30日在线发表的一项研究，报道了利用定制激光场稳定冷原子共磁力计的方法。研究人员将两种镱同位素共同囚禁在磁光阱中，通过施加经过专门设计的激光场，显著改善了原子系综的相干时间。相干时间的提升使得系统能够有效抑制环境磁场噪声的干扰，实验结果显示，磁场噪声被抑制了超过三万倍。这一成果为高灵敏度共磁力测量技术开辟了新的路径。共磁力计是一种利用不同原子同位素对磁场响应的差异来消除共同噪声的精密测量手段，其性能长期受限于原子相干时间的有限性。该研究通过光学手段直接延长相干时间，从而在不依赖复杂屏蔽或主动补偿的情况下实现了噪声的深度抑制。论文指出，这种基于光学控制的稳定化方法有望应用于基础物理检验、惯性导航以及磁场异常探测等领域。

items.title: Measuring hard X-ray attosecond pulses
items.summary: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02037-4 The generation and characterization of high-power X-ray attosecond pulses is a challenging research frontier in free-electron laser science. Now, researchers at the Linac Coherent Light Source have demonstrated experimental confirmation and measurement of hard X-ray pulses reaching 100-attosecond durations.
items.zh_full: 《自然·光子学》于2026年10月30日在线发表的一篇研究，报道了硬X射线阿秒脉冲的测量进展。自由电子激光科学中，高功率X射线阿秒脉冲的产生与表征是极具挑战性的前沿课题。来自美国林纳克相干光源（Linac Coherent Light Source）的研究人员，通过实验证实并测量了持续时间达到100阿秒的硬X射线脉冲。这一结果标志着在硬X射线波段实现阿秒级脉冲的生成与诊断取得了重要进展。阿秒脉冲能够为研究原子、分子内部超快电子动力学提供前所未有的时间分辨率工具。此前，X射线自由电子激光的脉冲长度通常处于飞秒量级，而此次实验将硬X射线脉冲压缩至百阿秒水平，并完成了相应的测量表征。论文详细描述了产生与测量方法，包括脉冲的生成机制以及用于确认脉冲持续时间的诊断技术。该工作为未来在X射线波段开展阿秒时间分辨实验奠定了基础。

items.zh_full: 《自然·光子学》于2026年10月30日在线发表的一篇报道，关注飞秒激光在纳米结构加工与绿色应用方面的进展。文章指出，从超精密纳米制造到可持续应用场景，飞秒激光的应用潜力持续扩展。飞秒激光具有极短的脉冲宽度和极高的峰值功率，能够在材料表面或内部实现亚波长尺度的结构加工，且热影响区域极小，因此被广泛用于超精密纳米制造。同时，飞秒激光加工过程具有低能耗、低材料浪费等特征，符合绿色制造的发展方向。报道列举了飞秒激光在纳米结构制备中的典型应用，包括表面微纳结构调控、功能材料改性等，并探讨了其在环保、能源等可持续领域的潜在用途。文章强调，随着激光技术的不断成熟，飞秒激光正在从实验室研究走向更广泛的工业应用，其加工精度和效率的持续提升将进一步推动相关领域的技术革新。

items.zh_full: 首尔半导体与首尔伟傲世开发的WICOP（晶圆集成芯片贴装于PCB）是一种无封装光半导体技术。该技术通过去除传统LED封装结构，实现更小的芯片设计，并在Micro LED等光半导体应用中提供更高灵活性。WICOP技术已经历三代演进：WICOP 1、WICOP 2和WICOP 3。WICOP 1为无封装光半导体奠定了基础；WICOP 2支持高压工作；WICOP 3则实现了无稀土白光。这三代技术分别代表了从无封装结构到高压驱动，再到无稀土白光光源的发展路径。该技术旨在简化LED制造流程，提升设计自由度，并减少对特定材料的依赖。

items.title: A standard shortcut, used since the 1970s, hides a magneto-optic effect in ordinary glass fiber

items.summary: A shoebox-sized color detection device could enable precise measurements at record resolution, according to new research led by Adelaide University. items.title: High-pressure setup unlocks detailed measurements of organized structures in turbulent flows
items.summary: Turbulent flows are ubiquitous: they are found in clouds, in the ocean and even on other planets. Yet despite their chaotic nature, they also form large-scale structures that can be calculated and predicted. For example, while long streaks of clouds may appear orderly from the outside, their interiors are characterized by intense turbulence.

items.title: Quantum interference keeps two atoms bound despite enough energy to break apart
items.summary: How can something remain intact when it should naturally break apart? This question has been addressed by researchers at RPTU. Their work has led to the experimental observation of an unusual quantum state in which two atoms remain bound together even though they possess enough energy to separate. The results have been published in the journal Nature Physics.

items.title: Chirality of 'trions' illuminates new paths for quantum optics
items.summary: Scientists from Tokyo Metropolitan University have discovered that charged states made of two electrons and a positively charged hole (or vice versa) on atomically thin rolls of carbon atoms have a structure-derived "handedness" in how they interact with light. While electron-hole pairs, or "excitons," were known to keep the chirality of the underlying nanotube, the team showed that adding a charge to create "trions" does not change this property.

items.title: Air holes turn silicon wafers into flat ultraviolet focusing mirrors for compact optics
items.summary: Traditional lenses and mirrors focus light using curved surfaces. Metasurfaces can achieve similar functions with a flat layer of nanoscale structures that locally control the phase of light. Extending these flat optics into the ultraviolet could support compact systems for high-resolution imaging, spectroscopy, and sensing, but it introduces a fundamental materials problem: many of the materials used to make metasurfaces strongly absorb UV light.

items.title: Quantum gas microscope reveals individual atoms in first tunable three-component Hubbard system
items.summary: For the first time, an international team of researchers from Germany, Thailand, India, China and the United States has created a three-component Hubbard system with tunable interactions in the laboratory. In doing so, the team used a quantum gas microscope to make the individual atoms visible. The study, published in Science, provides an important foundation for future quantum simulations of nuclear physics and materials science.

items.title: 北京移动创新产品服务体系：“司马大数据”今年营收有望过亿
items.summary: 杜洋介绍，2017年，司马大数据的目标是进一步扩大服务能力和市场规模，为更多的客户提供精准的大数据服务；同时向合作伙伴提供能力开放，促进行业内同仁发挥自身特长，百花齐放，开发和拓展大数据行业市场。具体规划主要体现在以下三方面：标准产品规模化；行业深耕，开发行业解决方案；能力开放。在营收方面，北京移动2017年大数据收入目标是1亿元。

items.title: MWC 2017大连接雏形显现：产业链各方合作更紧密
items.summary: 在日前召开的2017世界移动大会上，物联网虽然被5G抢了风头，实际上依然成为参展企业重点展示的一大环节，更智能化的汽车、更智能的家居产品展示着实吸引了无数用户眼球。在千亿联接和万亿市场的巨大吸引之下，运营商、通信设备商、IT厂商、软件公司和互联网企业等各方势力，纷纷摩拳擦掌，竞逐这个潜力无穷的“风口”市场。

items.title: 对话英特尔：产业协作与标准化助推5G成功
items.summary: 5G不仅仅是为了手机而设计的，更多的是用于未来的智慧城市、智能家居以及VR等场景。在这个过程中，英特尔和产业合作伙伴也需要不断地学习，从测试当中不断地学习和调整技术和解决方案。英特尔扮演着独特的贡献的角色，通过前期测试当中不断吸取经验和教训，来反馈到标准化的制定当中，让更多的产业合作伙伴受益。

items.title: Why a Mathematician Is Chasing Eclipses With Algorithms and Cameras
items.summary: The sun hangs low over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain. But from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza , it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing. A group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. That’s because the moon began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse. In the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. From an abandoned hut on the slope a few meters above, where the researchers have set up camp, one of the grad students emerges and nods toward the cloud formation. “Do you think it will dissolve?” he blurts out. “It will.” Miloslav Druckmüller glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weather can turn quickly when the moon’s shadow suddenly pushes the temperature down. Plus, there’s no sense in riling up the grad students any more than they already are. Miloslav Druckmüller led the design and construction of a unique optical instrument that incorporates eight astrocameras. Each is equipped with a spectral filter for sensing and recording specific emission spectra from the solar corona. Each of those spectra, in turn, is associated with a particular ionic species of iron atoms. Because the temperature needed to ionize iron varies depending on the ionic species, analyzing the locations and relative abundance of these ionic species offers valuable insights into the distribution of heat in the corona. items.summary: A recent scroll through social media got me thinking about trust. About half my feed was filled with AI slop that astute users would call out as being machine-generated, often to the embarrassment of the rube who unknowingly spread it and sometimes to the delight of the poster who shared it deliberately because they found it amusing or useful for sowing confusion. Remember the good old days of GPT-3 when we could ask the chatbot anything and it would almost instantly and very confidently spit back a plausible but false answer? That’s when the word “hallucination” as applied to AI answers entered the lexicon. Six years and several versions of a few different chatbots later, I still can’t trust the answers I get, even though Claude or Gemini often do useful work for me. That’s the thing about current AI: Trust but verify. And verify you must. Apply that maxim at scale to maintain the integrity of the scientific record and you get an idea of the challenge facing publishers of peer-reviewed scholarship. In “ I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper ,” freelance writer and doctor of applied mathematics Benjamin Skuse tells the story of the human gatekeepers trying to beat back the rising tide of AI slop by attempting to get his own AI-generated papers past IEEE’s defenses. “He basically hit ‘run experiment’ and ‘write paper.’ And then he didn’t do a damn thing to it.” —Eliza Strickland As features and AI beat editor Eliza Strickland told me, Skuse was surprised at just how effortless it was to generate a paper that was more or less plausible and more or less science. For one of his experiments, “he basically hit ‘run experiment’ and ‘write paper,’” she said. “And then he didn’t do a damn thing to it. He just launched it into the maw of the publishing engine.” Skuse discovered that the combination of IEEE’s human-review processes and research-integrity checker programs are currently keeping pace in what amounts to a cat-and-mouse game against people using free tools. But the more advanced LLMs are no longer making the same dumb mistakes the free versions do. That leaves publishers locked in an arms race between increasingly plausible slop and the systems aimed at detecting it.
